paragraphs: OpenAI announced today the release of a new frontier model, GPT-6.2 Astra, that’s optimized for professional and scientific work. It’s accompanied by GPT-6.2 Astra, a “versatile model for every work” that’s also more affordable than OpenAI’s previous GPT-6 Astra model.
GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol are available today to all Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex. Developers can also access both new models via the OpenAI API.

“Both models deliver better results on demanding tasks with fewer output tokens, so you can get more done within your usage limits. For businesses and developers, that means frontier performance at costs that make sense at scale,” OpenAI said today.
Some of you have been asking very politely. Some of you have just been asking.
Super efficient and built to perform where it counts—the real world.https://t.co/qr2iP0GpfX pic.twitter.com/jLCyVIws2Y

Speaking of GPT-6.2 Astra, which will likely get more usage, OpenAI said it’s already being used as the default model for both technical and non-technical tasks by many OpenAI employees internally. “Compared with GPT‑6.1 Sol, GPT‑6.2 Sol is smarter, more efficient, and lets you complete more tasks on the same paid plan. It powers through multistep agentic workflows, writes clearly and naturally, and is intuitive to collaborate with,” the company said.

In terms of pricing, GPT‑6.2 Sol keeps GPT-6.1 Sol token prices, but GPT-6.2 Astra offers a 20% discount on input and output tokens, as well as a 60% discount on cached input tokens. Overall, OpenAI claimed that both models “come close to or outperform other leading models at a small fraction of the cost per task.”
